subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Compared with adult stem cells, embryonic stem cells can:
options: Differentiate into a wider range of cell types
questions.explain: Embryonic stem cells can form almost any cell type, whereas adult stem cells form a more limited range.

options: A cell that can no longer divide
A cell that has lost its nucleus
An undifferentiated cell that can divide to form different types of cell
questions.explain: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells able to divide and differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.q: How many cells are produced from one parent cell by mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells (meiosis, not mitosis, makes four).

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical human male?
questions.explain: Human males have XY sex chromosomes, while females have XX.
Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry genes.
Meiosis produces four non-identical haploid gametes, each with half the normal number of chromosomes.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: What are the main purposes of mitosis in the body?
questions.explain: Mitosis is used for growth, repair/replacement of cells, and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: Which of these is an ethical concern raised against the use of embryonic stem cells?
options: Embryos that could develop into a person are destroyed
They are too easy to grow
questions.explain: A key objection is that obtaining embryonic stem cells involves destroying embryos.

questions.q: Different versions of the same gene are called:
questions.explain: Alleles are different forms of a gene, for example for eye colour.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the physical characteristics
Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the alleles
questions.explain: Genotype is the combination of alleles, while phenotype is the observable characteristic produced.

questions.q: A risk of using stem cells in medical treatment is that:
options: They cannot divide in the body
Cultured cells may become contaminated with a virus and pass it to the patient
questions.explain: Stem cells grown in the lab may be contaminated with viruses that could be transferred to the patient.
